back: A member is created in your tenant and carries your domain; a guest is invited from outside and keeps their home identity. Guests get a restricted set of default directory permissions. Keyword: user type.

Membership is computed from a rule over user or device attributes and re-evaluated when attributes change. Requires Entra ID P1, and one rule targets users or devices, never both. Keyword: membership rule.
A security group grants access to resources. A Microsoft 365 group also provisions a shared mailbox, calendar, and SharePoint site. Keyword: group type.
Writes a cloud password reset back to on-premises Active Directory in a hybrid tenant. Without it, only the cloud copy of the password changes. Keyword: hybrid.
Management group, subscription, resource group, resource. Assignments are inherited downward and are additive — you cannot subtract a permission at a lower scope. Keyword: inheritance.
Contributor manages resources but cannot grant access. Owner is Contributor plus role assignment. User Access Administrator manages access only. Keyword: role assignment.

Blocks specified actions even when a role assignment allows them. Deny always beats allow, and deny assignments are created by Azure (Blueprints, managed apps), not by administrators. Keyword: precedence.

Deny blocks a deployment; Audit flags it; Append and Modify change properties on the way in; DeployIfNotExists provisions a missing resource. Modify and DeployIfNotExists need a managed identity. Keyword: effect.
Applies a Modify or DeployIfNotExists effect to resources that already exist. Policy effects otherwise only fire on create or update. Keyword: retrospective.
CanNotDelete allows changes but blocks deletion. ReadOnly blocks changes too — including listing storage account keys, because that call is a write. Keyword: most restrictive wins.
No. Tagging a resource group does not tag the resources in it. Use Azure Policy with a Modify effect and a remediation task to push tags down. Keyword: not inherited.
Alerts when actual or forecast spend crosses a threshold at a scope. It never stops spending or shuts anything down. Keyword: alert only.
Globally unique across all of Azure, 3–24 characters, lowercase letters and numbers only — it becomes a public DNS label. Keyword: global DNS.
LRS: three copies, one datacentre. ZRS: three copies across zones in one region. GRS: async copy to the paired region. GZRS: both. Keyword: blast radius.

front: When is the secondary region readable?
back: Only with RA-GRS or RA-GZRS. Plain GRS and GZRS replicate but expose no readable secondary endpoint. Keyword: read access.
Holds a SAS token's expiry and permissions server-side on the container, so deleting or changing the policy revokes every token bound to it. An ad-hoc SAS cannot be revoked. Keyword: revocation.
A SAS signed with Entra credentials rather than the account key, so it can be revoked by revoking the identity and leaves no shared secret in play. Keyword: Entra-signed.
Two keys exist so you can rotate one at a time: move clients to key 2, regenerate key 1, move back. Rotating both at once breaks every client. Keyword: two keys.
Hot, cool (30-day minimum), cold (90-day), archive (180-day, offline). Archive must be rehydrated before reading and is set per blob only. Keyword: minimum retention.
Soft delete recovers deleted blobs and containers for a retention period. Versioning keeps a previous copy on every overwrite. Deletion versus modification. Keyword: which loss.
Daily-evaluated rules with filters and actions that move blobs between tiers or delete them after N days since creation or last modification. Keyword: automation.
Asynchronously copies block blobs from a source container to a destination. Requires change feed and versioning enabled on the source account. Keyword: change feed.
schema, contentVersion, parameters, variables, resources, outputs. Parameters take values at deploy time; variables are computed inside. Keyword: declarative.
Incremental (default) leaves untemplated resources alone. Complete deletes anything in the resource group that is not in the template. Keyword: deletion risk.
Bicep is a DSL that compiles to the same ARM JSON — same capability, less syntax. Decompile JSON to Bicep, build Bicep to JSON. Keyword: transpiles.

front: Why is a VM size greyed out?
back: The size is not available on the current hardware cluster. Stop and deallocate the VM to move it to a cluster that offers it. Keyword: deallocate.
Local scratch storage whose contents are lost on deallocation or host maintenance. Never store anything you need on it. Keyword: ephemeral.

front: Azure Disk Encryption vs encryption at host
back: ADE encrypts inside the guest with BitLocker or dm-crypt. Encryption at host encrypts on the Azure host, covers the temp disk and caches, and must be enabled on the subscription first. Keyword: where.
A set spreads VMs across fault and update domains in one datacentre. Zones are physically separate datacentres in a region. A VM joins one or the other, never both. Keyword: blast radius.
Uniform treats instances as interchangeable from one model. Flexible places individually configurable VMs across fault domains and is the current default. Keyword: mode.

front: Scale up vs scale out in App Service
back: Scaling up changes the plan's pricing tier and instance size. Scaling out changes the instance count. Autoscale needs Standard or above. Keyword: tier vs count.
Exchanges the routing between a staging slot and production, so the release is atomic and already warm. Swapping back is the rollback. Keyword: warm-up.
ACI runs a container now, with no orchestrator, billed per second. Container Apps adds ingress, revisions, traffic splitting, and event-driven scale to zero. Keyword: orchestration.
Azure reserves five per subnet: network, gateway, two DNS, broadcast. A /29 gives three usable addresses and is the smallest allowed. Keyword: minus five.
GatewaySubnet for a virtual network gateway, AzureBastionSubnet for Bastion, AzureFirewallSubnet for Azure Firewall. The names are exact. Keyword: reserved name.
No. A–B and B–C does not give A–C. Use a hub NVA with user-defined routes, or Virtual WAN. Keyword: non-transitive.
The hub sets 'allow gateway transit' and the spoke sets 'use remote gateways', letting the spoke reach on-premises through the hub's gateway without one of its own. Keyword: pair of settings.
Only one side of the link was created. A peering is two objects and both must exist before it reaches Connected. Keyword: both halves.

front: Standard public IP is secure by default
back: Inbound traffic is denied unless an NSG rule allows it, and the address is always static. Basic behaved the opposite way and is retired. Keyword: deny by default.

front: No outbound internet from a VM
back: A VM behind a Standard internal load balancer with no public IP has no default outbound access. Add a NAT gateway to the subnet. Keyword: NAT gateway.
A route table attaches to a subnet, never to a network interface. One table per subnet; one table can serve many subnets. Keyword: subnet-level.
Longest prefix match wins first. On a tie, user-defined routes beat BGP routes, which beat system routes. Keyword: specificity.
A network virtual appliance's NIC must have IP forwarding enabled or it silently drops traffic that is not addressed to it. Keyword: silent drop.
Priority 100–4096, lowest number evaluated first, first match wins. The filter is stateful, so an allowed inbound flow's reply needs no outbound rule. Keyword: stateful.

front: NSG on subnet and NIC together
back: Inbound is filtered by the subnet NSG then the NIC NSG; outbound runs the reverse. Traffic must be allowed by both. Keyword: both must allow.
Lets an NSG rule name a logical group of network interfaces instead of IP ranges, so 'web tier to database tier' keeps working as machines change. Keyword: logical grouping.

A service endpoint keeps the service's public IP and restricts it to named subnets. A private endpoint gives the service a private IP in your subnet, works from on-premises, and needs a private DNS zone. Keyword: private IP.
Points a DNS record at an Azure resource and tracks it, so deleting the target removes the record instead of leaving a dangling name. Also solves CNAME-at-apex. Keyword: dangling DNS.
An instance failing its probe leaves rotation; if all instances fail, the pool is unreachable and the outage looks total. An HTTP probe needs a 200. Keyword: probe failure.
Metrics are numeric, one-minute granularity, collected automatically, kept 93 days. Logs are varied records that must be routed somewhere first and are queried with KQL. Keyword: automatic vs routed.
Per-resource configuration that sends log and metric categories to a Log Analytics workspace, storage account, event hub, or partner. Without one, the workspace is empty. Keyword: routing.

front: Collecting memory or disk space from a VM
back: Guest-level data is not platform telemetry. It needs the Azure Monitor Agent plus a data collection rule. Keyword: agent required.
A metric alert condition that learns the metric's baseline instead of using a fixed number — the right choice when normal varies by time of day. Keyword: baseline.
A reusable named set of notifications and actions referenced by alert rules, so an on-call change is made once rather than per rule. Keyword: reusable.
An alert processing rule suppresses notifications for a scope and window without touching the rules. Disabling rules stops evaluation and is easy to forget to undo. Keyword: processing rule.

front: IP flow verify vs next hop
back: IP flow verify says whether a five-tuple is allowed and names the NSG rule. Next hop says where a packet would actually be sent. Blocked versus misrouted. Keyword: which symptom.

front: Recovery Services vault vs Backup vault
back: Recovery Services covers Azure VMs, MARS/MABS, Azure Files, SQL and SAP HANA in a VM. Backup vault covers blobs, disks, PostgreSQL, and Kubernetes. Keyword: workload.
Backup restores lost or corrupted data from recovery points. Site Recovery replicates whole machines so they can be brought up in another region. Keyword: data vs region.
